rationale: Evidence from iteration 6 (outer sensors at x = ±0.06, sensor_size 0.016, kp 7.0, kd 0.2, ki 0.0; score 64.74, the best raced design). The s-bend progress rose from the flat 0.04 seen in iterations 0 to 5 to 0.14, and its line_loss_events fell from 1.0 to 0.0. The outer-sensor reach was therefore the limit at the bend, as the Evaluator's branch (a) predicted. The s-bend max_error is 0.0605, essentially at the 0.06 m off-track limit. Oval progress fell from 0.30 to 0.22 and oval line_loss_events fell to 0. Slalom is unchanged at progress 0.10 with one line loss per run. The main remaining cost is steering_oscillation, which is 0.159 on the oval and 0.173 on the s-bend, against about 0.07 at kp 5 to 6. Following the Evaluator's plan (a), this candidate keeps the ±0.06 outer sensors and sensor_size 0.016, and changes one group only: kp from 7.0 to 6.5 with kd kept at 0.2. Expected result: steering_oscillation falls to roughly 0.13 to 0.15 on the oval and s-bend, max_error stays near or below 0.06 m, and s-bend progress holds near 0.14. Oval progress may dip slightly (about 0.18 to 0.22), which is the trade-off to watch. Hypotheses: (1) if s-bend progress holds and oscillation drops, the next single-group revision is line_loss search_right or a test of the slalom line loss. (2) If s-bend progress falls back toward 0.04, kp is contributing to the bend stall, so return to kp 7.0 and address oscillation with kd. (3) If the robot tracks without off_track but completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise base_speed to 1.6 in a later single-group revision. Slalom remains the weakest track (line_loss 1.0 per run, progress 0.10), so its line-loss behaviour is the next thing to examine.
